props.gloss_en: Rav: an orla caper-bush outside the Land -- one discards the berries and eats the buds
the mishnah: over the leaves and fronds of the caper one says borei pri haadama, and over the berries and the buds borei pri haetz
R' Eliezer: the caper-bush is tithed of its fronds, berries and buds
R' Akiva: only the berries are tithed, because that is the fruit
whoever is lenient [in orla] in the Land, the halakha follows him outside the Land, but not in the Land
the leniency abroad holds for orla too (Torah law in the Land), not only for tree-tithes (rabbinic even in the Land): no decree is made abroad
Mar bar Rav Ashi discarded the berries and ate the buds [of an orla caper]
Beit Shammai: the caper-bush is kilayim in a vineyard
Beit Hillel: the caper-bush is not kilayim in a vineyard
both schools agree the caper-bush is liable to orla
Beit Shammai are uncertain [whether the caper is a vegetable or a tree], and are stringent here [kilayim] and here [orla]
the mishnah: uncertain orla is forbidden in the Land, permitted in Syria, and abroad one may go down and buy it provided he does not see it picked
R' Akiva against R' Eliezer, we act as he says; Beit Shammai against Beit Hillel is no mishnah
'you shall treat its fruit as orla' (Lev 19:23): 'et piryo' includes what is secondary to its fruit, namely the fruit's protection
Rava (1): something is protection for the fruit only if it is there both detached and attached; the bud is there only while attached
the mishnah: a pomegranate's crown joins [it for the measure of tumah], and its flower does not
the mishnah on orla: the rinds of a pomegranate and its flower, nutshells and pits are liable to orla
Rava (2): something is protection for the fruit only if it is there when the fruit ripens; this bud is not
Rabba bar Avuh: these orla date-coverings are forbidden, since they became protection for the fruit
Rav Nachman holds like R' Yosei, and the Rabbanan dispute him -- so the date-coverings do not tell against Rava's criterion for the Rabbanan
R' Yosei: the grape-bud (semadar) is forbidden [as orla], because it is fruit
Beit Shammai: in the Sabbatical year one may not cut any tree from when it produces [fruit]
Beit Hillel: carobs from when they form chains, vines from misheyegaru, olives from when they blossom, and all other trees from when they produce
Rav Asi: misheyegaru is the unripe grape (boser), it is the kernel, it is the white bean
Rava (3): something is protection for the fruit only where removing it kills the fruit; here removing the bud does not
there was an incident: they removed a pomegranate's flower and the pomegranate withered; they removed a caper-fruit's flower and the caper-fruit survived
since the buds are not fruit for orla, they are not fruit for blessings either: over them one says not borei pri haetz but borei pri haadama
Rav Sheshet: over peppers one says shehakol
Rava: over peppers one says nothing
Rava: one who chews peppers on Yom Kippur is exempt
Rava: one who chews ginger on Yom Kippur is exempt
R' Meir: 'a tree for food' (Lev 19:23) comes to include a tree whose wood and fruit taste alike -- the pepper tree -- to teach that peppers are liable to orla
R' Meir: and to teach that the Land of Israel lacks nothing, as it says 'a land where you shall eat bread without scarceness, you shall lack nothing in it' (Deut 8:9)
Rava: the himalta that comes from India is permitted, and over it one says borei pri haadama
Rav Yehuda: over chavitz kedera and daysa one says shehakol nihye bidvaro
Rav Kahana: over them one says borei minei mezonot
over plain daysa all agree: borei minei mezonot; they dispute daysa made like chavitz kedera
Rav Yehuda's reason: the honey is primary
Rav Kahana's reason: the flour is primary
Rav and Shmuel: anything that contains any of the five species, one says over it borei minei mezonot

supports.gloss_en: הוה עובדא: the pomegranate died without its flower, the caper-fruit survived without its flower
ומדלגבי ערלה לאו פירא נינהו, לגבי ברכות נמי לאו פירא נינהו
ואזדא רבא לטעמיה, דאמר רבא: כס פלפלי ביומא דכפורי פטור -- chewing peppers is not eating
כוותיה דרב כהנא מסתברא, דרב ושמואל דאמרי תרוייהו: כל שיש בו מחמשת המינין מברכין עליו בורא מיני מזונות

objections.gloss_en: למימרא דאביונות פירי וקפריסין לאו פירי? ורמינהו: ...ועל האביונות ועל הקפריסין אומר בורא פרי העץ -- the mishnah treats the buds as fruit too

answered_by.gloss_en: הוא דאמר כרבי עקיבא -- Rav follows R' Akiva, for whom only the berries are the caper's fruit

objections.gloss_en: מאי דעתך, כרבי עקיבא דמיקל? ולעביד מר כבית שמאי דמקילי טפי! דתנן: צלף, בית שמאי אומרים כלאים בכרם... -- and (36a.24-36b.1) מכל מקום, for Beit Shammai it is safek orla, and ותנן: safek orla abroad may be bought -- so abroad even the berries could be eaten

answered_by.gloss_en: רבי עקיבא במקום רבי אליעזר עבדינן כוותיה, ובית שמאי במקום בית הלל אינה משנה (= p_bs_bimkom_bh)

objections.gloss_en: הא גופא קשיא: Beit Shammai's kilayim makes the caper a vegetable, yet both agree it is liable to orla, which makes it a tree

answered_by.gloss_en: Beit Shammai are in doubt, and are stringent both here and here (= p_bs_mesupakim)

objections.gloss_en: ותיפוק ליה דנעשה שומר לפרי -- the bud protects the fruit, and 'et piryo' includes the fruit's protection, so the buds should be forbidden as orla

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא אמר רבא: protection is only what the fruit dies without; removing the bud does not kill the caper-fruit (= p_rava_meit_peira; his answers at 36b.4 and 36b.6 fell -- see header)

objections.gloss_en: איתיביה אביי: the pomegranate's flower does not join for tumah -- מדקאמר... אלמא דלאו אוכל הוא -- yet ותנן גבי ערלה: the pomegranate's flower is liable to orla
איני?! והאמר רב נחמן אמר רבה בר אבוה: orla date-coverings are forbidden as protection; ושומר לפירי אימת הוי -- בכופרא, and still he calls them protection

answered_by.gloss_en: רב נחמן סבר לה כרבי יוסי, ופליגי רבנן עליה (= p_rn_kerabbi_yosei; itself brought down at 36b.9-10)

objections.gloss_en: ובשאר אילני מי פליגי רבנן עליה? והתנן... ושאר כל האילנות משיוציאו; and (36b.10) מאן שמעת ליה דאמר בוסר אין סמדר לא -- רבנן, וקתני שאר כל האילנות משיוציאו: in other trees the Rabbanan too count the earliest fruit
פול הלבן סלקא דעתך?! -- a grape is never a white bean

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא אימא: שיעורו כפול הלבן -- its size is that of a white bean

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: R' Meir counts the pepper tree as 'a tree for food', liable to orla -- so peppers are food

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא ברטיבתא, הא ביבשתא -- R' Meir speaks of fresh peppers, Rava of dry

objections.gloss_en: אמרי ליה רבנן למרימר: כס זנגבילא ביומא דכפורי פטור? והא אמר רבא: Indian himalta is permitted and one says borei pri haadama over it

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: הא ברטיבתא, הא ביבשתא -- the blessing is over fresh, the exemption over dry
